summary: 3D Object COMP that contains POP/SOP-style shape networks and is rendered by a Render TOP. It combines object transforms, material assignment, render flags, light masks, and GPU instancing controls for polygons, points, particles, line strips, and custom shader-driven instance attributes.

common_gotchas: Most Geometry workflows keep the internal POP/SOP Render Flag and Display Flag together; a shape can appear in the Geometry Viewer yet not be rendered if only the Display Flag is on.
Every Geometry component needs a Material assigned for shaded rendering; Render TOPs draw the geometry, but the Geometry COMP owns the material binding.
Light Mask filters only lights that are also listed in the Render TOP, so a light must match both the Geometry COMP Light Mask and the Render TOP Lights parameter.
Instance attributes can come from TOP RGBA channels, CHOP channels, DAT rows, or SOP attributes; mismatched row/sample/attribute choices are a common cause of wrong instance counts or transforms.
Instance Textures select among multiple TOPs by Texture Index; this is different from selecting a slice in a 3D Texture or 2D Texture Array.
Custom instance attributes are for GLSL MAT access through TDInstanceCustomAttrib0() and related functions; those custom attributes are ignored by other materials such as the PBR MAT.
Render visibility is the logical AND of this component's Render parameter and its Render Flag, so both must allow rendering.
